problem: Learning-based MultiON baselines (RNN, neural feature maps, memory networks) need heavy training and generalize poorly to unseen environments and tasks. A simple classical modular pipeline had not been shown to compete on Multi-Object Goal navigation.
motivation: Multi-object goal navigation requires locating goals and caching spatial information over long horizons. Classical projective-geometry mapping plus planning needs no training and is transferable to new environments. It could match learning-based agents on success rate.
key_idea: Build a training-free modular agent that back-projects depth into an occupancy map and colour-thresholded goal detections into a goal map, then plans to the goal with D* if it is localized and explores by frontiers otherwise.
insight: A classical, training-free pipeline achieves the highest success (0.62) and progress (0.71) among the compared methods, beating the learned AuxTaskMap (0.57 / 0.70). It is less path-efficient (SPL 0.34 vs 0.36; PPL 0.39 vs 0.45), consistent with the known pattern that classical methods succeed more often but take less efficient paths. Localizing all target objects, not only the current goal, avoids redundant exploration. There is no ablation, so these explanations are not tested.
method: Mapping: back-projects the depth image into an egocentric top-down occupancy grid (vacant/occupied/unexplored), transforms it into the allocentric frame using the GPS/compass pose, and overlays it on the global map (M=N=550).

Goal Localization: marks pixels within epsilon (0.001) of each target cylinder colour, removes connected components smaller than delta=50 pixels, and projects the remaining pixels with depth into an n-channel top-down goal map. All n target colours are localized, not only the current goal.
Policy (goal known): if the current goal's map channel is non-empty, targets the mean location of its non-zero pixels and plans with D*.
Policy (goal unknown): explores using frontier-based exploration on the occupancy map until the goal is seen.
Found action: the Found action is called within 1.5 m of the target; mapping and goal localization run concurrently with the policy.

setting.backbone: none (classical: projective geometry mapping, colour thresholding, D*, frontier exploration)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: Move Forward, Turn Left, Turn Right, Found
setting.privileged: noiseless GPS/compass pose; goals are uniquely coloured cylinders detectable by colour thresholding

numbers.extra: CVPR 2021 MultiON challenge setting, 3 goals; the split name is not stated explicitly in the paper

numbers_note: MultiON is not in the canonical benchmark list, so it is given as bench 'MultiON'. Metrics are printed as decimals and copied as such. The split is not explicitly named (challenge evaluation, ranked 2nd in the challenge).
results: SGoLAM reaches Success 0.62 and Progress 0.71, beating the best learned baseline AuxTaskMap (0.57 / 0.70) with no training. AuxTaskMap is better on PPL (0.45 vs 0.39) and SPL (0.36 vs 0.34). It ranked 2nd in the CVPR 2021 MultiON challenge.
limitations: Path efficiency (SPL/PPL) is lower than the best learned method.
Relies on noiseless GPS/compass and simple colour-based detection of uniquely coloured cylinders, so it may not transfer to realistic objects or noisy sensors.
Only a single comparison table; no ablations or failure analysis.
